citation: Dietz, Rising, Stoerk and Wagner (2021). Economic impacts of tipping points in the climate system. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 118(34), e2103081118. https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2103081118
description: META 2021 is an integrated climate-economy model published by the OpenModels group to study climate tipping points and the social cost of carbon. It simulates country-level emissions, temperature, sea-level rise and market or non-market damages, including eight tipping processes considered in its research paper. Users provide socioeconomic scenarios, model parameters and tipping assumptions; outputs are damage and climate trajectories or social-cost estimates by scenario. Geographic coverage is country-level and global, not an individual utility or road network. GPL-3.0 source, a Mimi/Julia implementation and an Excel version are public. The Excel workflow additionally requires the commercial @RISK extension; the README says the Mimi version supports further development. A limitation is that its aggregate damage functions cannot validate local asset fragility. META can inform long-run climate risk assumptions in infrastructure planning. The related catalogue IPCC AR6 scenario database supplies distinct pathway inputs. No spreadsheet, solver or scenario data was downloaded.
name: META 2021 climate tipping-point model
